quoted_clause: with the ~500-token prefill included the total request rate is ~71 rps at 100% MFU (~21–28 rps at 30–40% MFU), so r = 50 in the worked example below is an optimistic decode-only illustration
observed: r = 50 is a total request-rate assumption (requests per second), not a decode-only rate. It is below the 100%-MFU total ceiling of ~71 rps and above the 30–40% MFU total range, so calling it “decode-only” is misleading.
correction: Change to: “so r = 50 in the worked example below is an optimistic total-rate illustration (below the 100%-MFU total ceiling of ~71 rps but above the 30–40% MFU total range); the measured per-host total rate must replace it before the burst budget is trusted.”
acceptance_test: The text no longer implies that r = 50 is a decode-only token or request rate.

fix_instruction: ch23:113 - replace 'optimistic decode-only illustration' with 'optimistic total-rate illustration (below the ~71 rps total ceiling)'.

page_hint: Ch 23 §8 mini-case, mirror restatement and "The burst buffer, spelled out"
quoted_clause: a 7B-class model on one on-prem GPU, resolving baseline tickets under 3 s, with a 200-rps burst buffer ... a decode-only ceiling of 100% MFU (≤141 rps — 7B FP16, ~500 output tokens/request, H100); with the ~500-token prefill included the *total* request rate is ~71 rps at 100% MFU (~21–28 rps at 30–40% MFU), so r = 50 in the worked example below is an optimistic decode-only illustration
observed: The mini-case's own arithmetic shows that one H100 sustains at most ~71 req/s at a physically impossible 100% MFU (and ~21–28 req/s at the 30–40% MFU the book uses elsewhere), yet the mirror restatement commits the scope to "one on-prem GPU" with "a 200-rps burst buffer". The worked burst drain (r = 50) is itself above the realistic single-GPU rate, so the 3 s drain conclusion rests on a rate the chapter has already flagged as unattainable. The chapter's conclusion (bursts under a degraded SLO) is sound, but the committed scope statement is not.
correction: State the burst capacity the committed topology can actually absorb (one GPU at 21–28 req/s; N GPUs at N x that), and either size the burst buffer to the real drain rate or state the degraded-mode SLO in terms of the real r. The mirror restatement should say "one on-prem GPU serving ~5 rps average, with the 200-rps burst admitted under a queue-and-drain degraded mode at the measured single-GPU rate of ~25 req/s", and the burst arithmetic should be re-run at that r.
acceptance_test: The r used in the burst arithmetic is at or below the rate the committed topology can sustain at the book's own planning MFU, and the mirror restatement's burst claim is consistent with it.
verdict_evidence: ch23:113 prints <=141 rps decode-only, ~71 with prefill, 21-28 at 30-40% MFU, then works r=50 (50x14 TFLOP / 989 = 70.8% MFU); at r=25 a 1 s 200-rps burst queues 175 and drains 7 s not 3 s; :111 commits to one GPU.
fix_instruction: Re-run the ch23:113 burst arithmetic at the real single-GPU rate (~21-28 rps) and restate :111's one-GPU scope against that r.
